issue: Under Section 404 of the First Step Act, may a district court reduce the sentence on a non-covered offense that was grouped with a covered crack cocaine offense for Guidelines purposes, where the covered offense effectively controlled the aggregate sentence?

sides.position: The First Step Act bars a district court from reducing the sentence on a non-covered offense, even if it was grouped with a covered offense and the covered offense effectively controlled the sentence.
cases: United States v. Mannie, 971 F.3d 1140 (10th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Gladney, 44 F.4th 1253 (10th Cir. 2022)

sides.position: Section 404(b) of the First Step Act does not bar a court from reducing the sentence for a non-covered offense that was grouped with covered offenses and included in the resulting aggregate sentence.
cases: United States v. Hudson, 967 F.3d 605 (7th Cir. 2020)

this_court: The Tenth Circuit follows Mannie and holds that the First Step Act prohibits reducing the sentence on a non-covered offense even when grouped with a covered offense that effectively controlled the sentence.
quote: We note that this holding in Mannie created a circuit split because, approximately a month before Mannie was issued, the Seventh Circuit held that Section 404(b) of the First Step Act “does not bar a court from reducing [the sentence for] a non-covered offense” in cases where the non-covered offense “was grouped with [the] covered offenses for sentencing, and the resulting aggregate sentence included . . . sentences for both the [non-covered] and covered offenses.”
cite: United States v. Gladney, 44 F.4th 1253 (10th Cir. 2022)
